references.text: Joseph gives credit to God for his ability to interpret dreams, which prepares Pharaoh to understand that it is God who reveals the future through the dream.
Joseph repeats and expands on the point from verse 25: God has shown Pharaoh what he must do. The message of the dream is a single revelation from God.
Joseph explains that the dream was repeated twice because the matter is firmly decided by God, and He will soon carry it out. This further clarifies that the dream is God's revelation.
Joseph interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's servants and points out that interpretations belong to God—the same principle as in 41:25.
Daniel explains to King Nebuchadnezzar that there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets and has shown the king what will happen—a strong parallel to Joseph's words to Pharaoh.
The Lord God does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets—a principle demonstrated in practice when God reveals His plans to Pharaoh through Joseph.
Both verses emphasize that dream interpretation is exclusively God's work, not human wisdom.
Pharaoh's acknowledgment confirms Joseph's claim that it is God who has revealed the truth.
